Same game engine as 3 but with way better story and characters.

The plot: it understands how to create plot hooks, interesting characters, factions, progression, etc.

The characters: much more endearing, and frankly, I can still write paragraphs on the player companions, but would be hard pressed to do the same for FO3.

The actual game mechanics: Turns out the team that actually developed the first Fallout games would understand how items that would boost stats would fit better into the game. They also understand the proper progression of weapons/levels vs enemies.

The factions: They are in the world, and their story to that point make sense. And this also plays into the above with the actual game mechanics.

The mods: better game, means people have put together just a little bit more time in fleshing out the game. It also means you can make the Mojave Wasteland look like you want it to look, and New Vegas itself is "fixed" to how the developers initially imagined it.

The writing: FO, when it shines, gets darkly comic.

The setting: The different locals are just more memorable, and interesting. This is about the only thing FO4 learned from FONV.

NV uses the same base engine, and was forced to release quickly, and buggy. However, it was pretty much the game FO3 should have been, no holds barred.

Rain interrupted the siege, but on 21 March, immediately south of Krak des Chevaliers, Baibar's forces captured a triangular outwork possibly defended by a timber palisade. On 29 March, the attackers undermined a tower in the southwest corner causing it to collapse whereupon Baibars' army attacked through the breach.
